advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive per-cell tier coverage from the workflow (e.g. evaluate each step's `if:` against each cell) instead of asserting a hard-coded literal dict.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:186 `assert all(tiers == {"default", "integration"} for tiers in tiers_by_cell.values())`

Inverted-trace: if the workflow gated the default or integration step to only ubuntu 3.13 (dropping a tier from some cells), this assertion would still pass because the dict values are literals, not derived from `workflow`.
tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:182-183 assert only that a single default step and single integration step exist
tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:186 the tier-coverage assertion is a hard-coded literal, so the `if:`/step-gating dimension is never inspected
ABSENCE: no assertion reads step.get('if') for the default or integration step to confirm it runs unconditionally across the matrix
advisory.finding: The 'every cell runs both tiers' assertion is tautological: tiers_by_cell is a hard-coded dict {cell: {'default','integration'}} built independent of the parsed workflow, then asserted to equal {'default','integration'}. It can never fail and does not verify the change's central claim that all four matrix cells run both the default and integration tiers.
merged_from: The test asserts len(default_steps)==1 and len(integration_steps)==1 but never checks those steps have no `if:` guard restricting them to a subset of cells, so it cannot detect a step being gated to e.g. only Python 3.13 — leaving the 'all four cells run every tier' invariant unverified.
